messages:
maria: Quick sync — thinking about a minimal, local "escape hatch" for canary/A-B traffic so we can fail fast without a central arbiter. Goal: cheap, reliable fallback for latency spikes or probe regressions. Thoughts? :thinking:

sam: +1 to local-first. We had too much ops churn last quarter from central rollback flaps. Proposal: keep slow/failed decision at the edge proxy with a small, auditable policy pulled from config service. Edge can flip to fallback variant when probe error rate > X or p99 latency > Y for N seconds.

jon: Tradeoffs: local decisions reduce coordination but can cause split-brain (different nodes disagree). Need a safe convergence mechanism and TTL on local overrides. Also: how do we prevent noisy flaps if autoscaling changes pod counts?

sam: Agree. Mechanisms:
1) Override TTL (e.g., 60s) and exponential backoff before re-eval.
2) Emit a stamped event to central telemetry (not for decisioning) so we can correlate and postmortem.
3) Prefer prefix-safe KPIs (probe failures & synthetic checks) over raw 99th token latency which is noisy.

maria: Example policy I sketched for edge config:
```json
{
  "policy_version": "v1",
  "fallback_variant": "model-v1-fallback",
  "probe_kpis": {
    "synthetic_fail_rate": {"threshold": 0.05, "window_s": 30},
    "probe_p99_ms": {"threshold": 1200, "window_s": 60}
  },
  "override_ttl_s": 60,
  "backoff_mult": 2,
  "min_evaluate_interval_s": 15
n}
```
(yes, small example - default values up for debate)

jon: A couple of boundary decisions we should explicitize: who owns the "probe" instrumentation? infra or runtime team? If infra owns probes, we can guarantee consistent sampling across instances; if runtime owns them, probes can be context-aware.

maria: Good call. I think infra owns the generic health probes (synthetic & latency) and runtime owns feature-specific safety checks (e.g., hallucination detectors tied to eval sets). Edge policy should support combining both signals but weight infra probes higher for automated fallback.

infra-bot: [deploy-check] Canary policy schema validated for edge rollout. 0 warnings, 1 info (consider increasing min_evaluate_interval_s for high-churn clusters).

sam: Implementation-note: keep fallback switch atomic inside proxy request path: decide variant before selecting worker, and store active override in ephemeral local state (non-persistent). This avoids long-lived sticky mismatches when pods are evicted. Also allow manual operator breakglass via console push to central control which sets a forced override key that edges honor.

jon: For observability: surface a per-instance override metric and a sampled trace header when fallback applied (x-fallback-applied: instance-id:reason). That helps debugging distributed disagreements.

maria: Action items: 1) sam to draft edge policy proto + config schema (this week). 2) infra to write probe ownership doc and recommended thresholds (next week). 3) jon to add observability headers + metrics instrumentation plan (PR for review).

maria: Bonus constraint: prefer eventual parity with Dedicated/Private deployments (config pulled from customer control-plane) so same policy semantics apply across hosted and private. Not now-blocker but keep compatibility in schema. :white_check_mark:
